questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of basic strength of the following amines is
questions.solution:
I. Piperidine is the most basic. The $\mathrm{N}$ lone pair is in an $s p^3$ hybrid orbital and there is no resonance and due to $+I$ effect of alkyl group attached, it becomes more basic than $s p^3$ hybridised ammonia.
II. In pyridine, lonepair is in a $s p^2$ hybridised orbital but does not get involved in delocalisation. The $s p^2$ hybrid is smaller than $s p^3$, so there is a stronger attraction to nucleus, so less basic. III. $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is more basic as in ammonia, lone pair is localised and easily available for donation. Basic character is determined by ability to donate lone pair.
IV. The basicity of aniline is lower than basicity of ammonia as in aniline, the lone pair of electrons on $\mathrm{N}$ is involved in resonance with benzene ring. So, correct order of basic strength is $\text{ I }$>$\text{ III }$>$\text{ II }$>$\text{ IV. }$

questions.q:
The correct order of acidity of the following compounds is
(I) ${CH}_{3} - C ≡ CH$
(II) ${F}_{3}C - C ≡ CH$
(III) ${CH}_{3}C ≡ {CCH}_{3}$
(IV) ${CH}_{3}CH = {CHCH}_{3}$
questions.solution:
The acidity of unsaturated compounds can be best described by observing the substituted group. The compounds containing the substituted group having strong $- I$ effect or week $+ I$ will be more acidic than the compounds containing the substituted group having week $- I$ effect or strong $+ I$ effect.

This is in accordance with reactivity series of inductive effect.

So, the order of acidity in the following group of compounds will be:

$\left(II\right) > \left(I\right) > \left(III\right) > \left(IV\right)$

questions.q: The method, which is based on the principle that "different components of a mixture are differently adsorbed on an adsorbent" is called
questions.solution: Zone refining method The principle of zone refining is that the impurities in an ingot or ore of metal are more soluble in the melt state when compared to the corresponding solid state of the impurities.Vapour phase refining method This method is based on the principle that the impure metal is converted into a volatile compound and which can be collected elsewhere. It is then decomposed used to give back the pure metal.Liquation method This method is based on the lower melting point of the metal than the impurities and tendency of the molten metal to flow on the sloping surface.Chromatographic method This method is based on the principle, where molecules in mixture applied onto the surface or into the solid, and fluid stationary phase (stable phase) is separating from each other while moving with the air of a mobile phase. In this method, different components of a mixture are differently adsorbed on an adsorbent. Hence, correct option is chromatographic method.

Thus, option (4) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following are not aromatic?
questions.solution:
Key Idea Conditions for species to be an aromatic are:
(i) The aromatic structures follows Huckel's mule, i.e. species have $(4 n+2) \pi$-electrons in its structure. where, $n=$ integer $0,1,2,3, \ldots$. so on.
(ii) Should be planar ring structure.
(A) It follows Huckel's rule and has planar structure thus, is an aromatic $(\because n=1$, $\pi e^{-}=6$ ).
(B) It does not follow Huckel's rule ( $\because$ has $8 \pi$ electrons with $n=2$ ).
(C) It follows Huckel's rule and has planar structure. Thus, is an aromatic $(\because n=1$, $\left.\pi e^{-}=6\right)$.
(D) It follows Huckel's rule and has planar structure as it has $n=3 and 14 \pi$ electrons.
(E) It does not follow Huckel's rule, thus is not an aromatic compound $\left(n=1, \pi e^{-}=4\right)$.
(F) It also does not follow Huckel's rule. Thus, is not an aromatic $\left(n=0, \pi e^{-}=4\right.$ )
Hence, species (B), (E) and (F) are not aromatic and option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The decreasing order of acidic strength for following acids is
(A) $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$
(B) $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$
(C) $\mathrm{ClCH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$
(D) $\mathrm{Cl}_2 \mathrm{CHCOOH}$
questions.solution:
(b) Key Idea Acidic strength increases with presence of $E W G$ (i.e. groups show-I effect) and decreases with the presence of EDG (i.e. groups show $+I$ or hyperconjugation effect). More be the number and more close be the EWG to the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, more is the acidic strength.
(A) $\stackrel{2}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3-\stackrel{1}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{OOH}$, has only one EDG, i.e. (by hyperconjugation) one $\mathrm{CH}_3$ group is bonded with $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group.
(B) < smiles>CC(Cl)CC(=O)O < /smiles>
has one EWG
(i.e. $\mathrm{Cl}$ ) at $\mathrm{C}-3$ position and $\mathrm{CH}_3$, i.e. one $\mathrm{EDG}$ (by hyperconjugation) at $\mathrm{C}_3$-position.
(C) $\mathrm{Cl}-\stackrel{2}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_2-\stackrel{1}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{OOH}$, has one EWG (i.e. Cl-atoms) at $\mathrm{C}_2-$ position.
(D) $\mathrm{Cl}_2-\stackrel{2}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}-\stackrel{1}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{OOH}$, has two EWG's (i.e. two $\mathrm{Cl}$-atom) at $\mathrm{C}_2$-position.
Thus, order of acidic strength is
(D) > (C) > (B) > (A) and option (b) is the correct answer.
